text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar warns Basque Nationalist Party (PNV) that policy of dispersing Basque separatist prisoners is irreversible.
- Surgeon who operated on Pope John Paul II assures pontiff "will not die of cancer".
- Secretary general Angel Colom and member of parliament Pilar Rahola defect from Esquerra Republicana de Catalunya (ERC) to create new independent party.
- Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos reveals that Ernesto Saenz de Buruaga, director of news at state television, earns 35 million pesetas per year, three times more than predecessor.
EL MUNDO
- Catalan president Jordi Pujol demands fiscal pact with central government like Basque country's.
- Spanish pathologist confirms Pope only had appendicitis.
DIARIO 16
- Spanish housewives want pensions too.
- Government wants to avoid European sanction for budget hole.

- Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja says state is not affected by case of presumed ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) members Jose Antonio Lasa and Jose Ignacio Zabala, murdered by death squads in a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatists.
ABC
- Pope recovers from operation and experts confirm he does not have cancer.
CINCO DIAS
- Social Security needs 460 billion pesetas to pay pensions until end of year.
- Gross company profits fell 0.8 percent in first six months of year.
EXPANSION
- Government ready to lower cost of changing mortage loans.
- Rate cut boosts company results despite weak consumption.
- Catalan regional government to inject one billion pesetas into software group CCS.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Accounts tribunal reveals anomalies of more than 75 billion pesetas in state television accounts.
- British Nobel Economics prize for theory on assymetrical information.
- Latest Bank of Spain report says lower financial costs compensate for rise in wages.
- Banco Central Hispano imposes technological revolution on network and staff.
- Government wants to sell Casa to Aerospatiale or British Aerospace.
